summary: Jupiter's 16-year mahadasha is described in every source as one of the best periods when Jupiter is strong: honour and high position, wealth, vehicles, marriage and children, learning and religious life. When Jupiter is debilitated, combust, joined with malefics or in the 6th or 8th, the texts predict loss of home and position, worry and trouble to children, but BPHS limits the bad results to the opening years and makes the later part good.
common_outcomes: high position or authority, recognition from the government, vehicles and clothes, devotion to gods and Brahmins, happiness from spouse and children, success in religious rites (BPHS 47.45-48, when strong)
virtuous deeds, birth of children, honour from the ruler and praise from great men, fulfilment of desires (Phaladeepika 19.11)
new clothes, attendants, respect, children, wealth and friends, praise for one's sound speech (Phaladeepika 19.22)
rank, wealth, vehicles, clothes, royal goodwill, purity of heart, knowledge and its practice, wife and children (Jataka Parijata 18.110)
plenty of clothes, wealth, grain, status, house, relatives, success and the things one wants, when Jupiter is strong and well placed (Uttara Kalamrita, Results of the Major Periods)
rare_outcomes: separation from elders or teachers, ear disease, phlegm (kapha) disorders (Phaladeepika 19.22)
displeasure of rulers, illness, loss of courage, shortage of food and money, trouble from Brahmins, the father's anger, consumption, when Jupiter is a malefic for the chart (Uttara Kalamrita)
as the sixth dasa in the sequence from birth, Jupiter's period is called dangerous (Phaladeepika 20.24; Raman, HPA ch. XXIV rule 2)
loss of residence, distress to children, loss of cattle, and pilgrimage, when afflicted (BPHS 47.49-50)

by_area.personality: Purity of heart, diligence, sound speech and learning (Jataka Parijata 18.110; Phaladeepika 19.22). Raman ties the tone to Jupiter's sign: calm and spiritual in Scorpio, dissolute and selfish in Libra, mean motives in Capricorn (HPA pp. 255-257).
by_area.career: Attainment of high office, recognition from the government, success in ventures (BPHS 47.45-48); rank and royal goodwill (Jataka Parijata 18.110). Loss of position when Jupiter is afflicted (BPHS 47.49-50, Sanskrit gloss). Raman: promotion and public success in Cancer, trustee or responsible office in Aries, firm business in Taurus.
by_area.finance: Wealth, vehicles, clothes, grain and property when strong (BPHS 47.45-48; Uttara Kalamrita); loss of cattle and wealth when afflicted (BPHS 47.49-50, gloss); lack of money when Jupiter is a malefic (Uttara Kalamrita). Raman: unexpected wealth in Cancer, loss of wealth in Virgo and Aquarius.
by_area.health: Generally good when strong. Ear disease and phlegm disorders (Phaladeepika 19.22); illness and consumption when Jupiter is a malefic (Uttara Kalamrita); nervous trouble in Virgo, consumption in Aquarius (Raman).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from wife and children (BPHS 47.47; Jataka Parijata 18.110). Raman reverses this for Gemini, Virgo and Capricorn, where he predicts loss of or illness to the wife.
by_area.family: Birth of children and their welfare (Phaladeepika 19.11; BPHS 47.49); distress to children when Jupiter is afflicted (BPHS 47.50). Separation from elders (Phaladeepika 19.22); the father's anger when Jupiter is a malefic (Uttara Kalamrita).
by_area.spirituality: Devotion to gods and Brahmins, success in Vedic rites and study of Vedanta (BPHS 47.46-47); pilgrimages even in the afflicted case (BPHS 47.50). Raman: religious worship and philosophical discourse when Jupiter is in Scorpio. Rath: an atmakaraka Jupiter's period turns one to spiritual life, with little sorrow if Jupiter is exalted (Crux p. 312).

strengtheners: Jupiter exalted, in its own sign or moolatrikona (BPHS 47.45)
Jupiter in the 5th, 9th or 10th from the lagna (BPHS 47.45, Santhanam); in a kendra, the 11th or a trikona (Sanskrit gloss)
Jupiter in its own or exaltation navamsa (BPHS 47.45)
Jupiter retrograde (Phaladeepika 20.14 counts it with own and exalted signs)
Jupiter in the lagna or aspected or joined by benefics (BPHS 47.5, general rule)
Jupiter ruling the 5th or 9th (Raman, HPA ch. XXIV rule 11), or a kendra or trikona (Uttara Kalamrita, p. 155)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter debilitated, or in the 6th or 8th (BPHS 47.49; Santhanam); in the 8th or 12th (Sanskrit gloss)
Jupiter combust or joined with malefics (BPHS 47.49)
Jupiter in an enemy sign, debilitated, combust or in a dusthana (BPHS 47.6; Phaladeepika 20.14, 20.27)
Jupiter ruling kendras (Phaladeepika 20.50), or the 6th, 8th or 12th (Phaladeepika 20.22, 20.24; Uttara Kalamrita p. 155)
planets placed in the 6th from Jupiter (Rath, Crux p. 330, citing Sarvartha Chintamani)
Jupiter in Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Capricorn or Aquarius, by Raman's sign list (HPA pp. 255-257)
lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role matters: P.S. Sastri notes that Jupiter becomes a functional malefic for some lagnas (he names Taurus, Cancer and Libra) and that a benefic in the 6th, 8th or 12th or owning kendras can turn harmful (Uttara Kalamrita, notes p. 147). Phaladeepika 20.50 makes Jupiter as a kendra owner capable of harm and, if it also owns or occupies the 2nd or 7th, of causing death. None of the sources read gives a natal rule for Jupiter's mahadasha by house from the Moon; Phaladeepika 20.60-62 judge from the Moon by transit. PVR Narasimha Rao (after Sanjay Rath) takes the Sun as the reference for mahadasha results (Integrated Approach 16.5.3).

source_views.source: BPHS 47.3-6, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 576-577
source_views.view: General rules for all dashas: results follow the lord's strength; a lord in the first, second or third decanate gives its results at the start, middle or end, reversed if retrograde. Good if the lord is in the lagna, exalted, own or friendly sign; bad in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or in an enemy sign.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.44-51, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 583-584
source_views.view: Strong Jupiter (exalted, own sign, moolatrikona, in the 10th, 5th or 9th, own or exalted navamsa): high position, government recognition, vehicles, clothes, devotion, happiness from wife and children, success in sacrifices. Debilitated, combust with malefics, or in the 6th or 8th: loss of residence, anxiety, distress to children, loss of cattle, pilgrimage; the bad results come only at the start and the later part brings wealth and honours.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.44-51, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Strength listed as exalted, own sign, kendra, 11th or trikona, moolatrikona, exalted or own navamsa: kingdom, courage, fame, palanquins, children and spouse, generosity with food. Adverse if linked with debilitated or combust malefics in the 8th or 12th: loss of position, mental distress, harm to children, fear, loss of livestock and wealth, pilgrimage. Early part hard, middle and end good.

19.11: virtuous deeds, children, honour from the sovereign, praise from great men, vehicles, reunion with family and friends, fulfilled desires. 19.22: new clothes, attendants, respect, children, wealth, friends, admired speech; also separation from elders, ear disease and phlegm troubles.

Retrograde, own, exalted or friendly planets outside the dusthanas give good results; combust, debilitated or enemy-sign planets or those in dusthanas give bad ones (20.14, 20.27). Vargottama gives good results, combust or debilitated mixed (20.22). Jupiter's dasa as the sixth dasa is dangerous (20.24). Combustion equals debilitation (20.30). Strong 2nd and 7th lords or occupants cause death in their dashas (20.40). Jupiter owning kendras becomes harmful and, owning or occupying the 2nd or 7th, death-causing (20.50). A combust, debilitated or enemy-sign planet in a good sign or amsa gives mixed results, good in the latter part (20.57).

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.110 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, vol. II)
source_views.view: Rank, wealth, vehicles, apparel, royal goodwill, purity of heart, power, knowledge and its practice, wife and children.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita, ch. 'Results of the Major Periods of Planets', tr. P.S. Sastri, pp. 145, 147, 154-155 (verse numbers not legible in the scan)
source_views.view: Strong, well-placed Guru: clothes, endless wealth, grain, status, house, relatives, success, luxuries. As a malefic: royal displeasure, worry, disease, loss of courage, want of food and money, trouble from Brahmins, father's anger, consumption. Periods of kendra and kona lords are highly beneficial, of 2nd, 3rd and 11th lords average, of 6th, 8th and 12th lords troublesome. Translator's note: Jupiter is a functional malefic for some lagnas.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 230-233 and 255-257
source_views.view: Results vary with the dasa lord's strength, sign, aspects and navamsa and must not be applied verbatim. Jupiter's dasa is unfavourable if it is the sixth dasa; periods of 5th and 9th lords are good. Sign-wise: Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Leo, Scorpio, Sagittarius and Pisces give property, success, fame and harmony; Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Capricorn and Aquarius give loss of wife, children or property, ill health, enemies or disgrace.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), pp. 312, 330-331
source_views.view: Planets in the 6th house from Jupiter are very inimical throughout Jupiter's dasa and their harm comes out in their own sub-periods (citing Sarvartha Chintamani 1.125-126). Treat the dasa planet as a temporary lagna. The dasa of the atmakaraka can be hard and spiritual, but an exalted Jupiter keeps sorrow minimal (Osho example).

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 16.5, pp. 213-215
source_views.view: A planet gives the results promised by its positions in the divisional charts. By Rath's 'tripod of life', the Sun is the reference point for judging a mahadasha, the Moon for an antardasha and the lagna for a pratyantardasha.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, ch. on planetary periods, pp. 202-203
source_views.view: The major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects. The start of a benefic's major period sows seeds rather than giving fruit at once. The start of a period is the time for remedies: strengthen a weak benefic with its gem, propitiate a malefic with mantra or worship.

disagreements: BPHS (Santhanam) lists the 10th, 5th and 9th as good houses; the Sanskrit gloss lists any kendra, the 11th or a trikona. Santhanam's bad case is the 6th or 8th; the gloss has the 8th or 12th and links the affliction to debilitated or combust malefics. Phaladeepika 20.24 and Raman call Jupiter's dasa dangerous if it is the sixth in sequence, which BPHS does not mention. Raman's sign list makes Jupiter bad in Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Capricorn and Aquarius regardless of house, while BPHS judges by dignity and house only. Phaladeepika 20.14 treats retrogression as a strength; BPHS 47.4 uses it only to reverse the timing.
phrasing_guidance: Describe this as a growth period for learning, family, status and faith, scaled by Jupiter's strength. Where the chart shows affliction, say the opening years may be slower or more worrying and that the period improves later, as BPHS says. Do not predict the death of a spouse or children or the native's death; Raman's harsh sign results are best given as areas needing care.

effects: bad results mainly at the start; gains and honours later

remedies.remedy: at the start of the period, if Jupiter is benefic but weak, strengthen it with its gemstone; if it is malefic for the chart, propitiate it with mantra, ritual or worship (general rule for any period lord)

phases: BPHS 47.49-51: when Jupiter is afflicted the bad results fall at the start of the dasha only and the later part brings wealth and recognition (the Sanskrit gloss: early part hard with some gain through animals, middle and end happy). BPHS 47.3-4: Jupiter in the first, second or third decanate of its sign gives its results at the start, middle or end of the dasha, reversed if retrograde. Phaladeepika 20.57: a combust, debilitated or enemy-sign Jupiter in a good sign or amsa gives its good effects in the latter part. Frawley: the opening of a benefic's major period sows seeds; the fruit comes later.
